What to expect

This is reflection, not judgment.

The process recognizes what you have built, surfaces opportunities, and asks honest questions so future AI decisions rest on a stronger foundation.

  • Stop and resume at any time
  • Decline or defer any question
  • Keep consequential decisions human-led

Why this exists

AI should solve a business problem—not become one.

Many AI efforts stall because organizations start with a tool before clarifying the customer need, workflow, data, decision rights, success measures, and human safeguards.

This framework slows down that first step just enough to make later decisions clearer, safer, and more useful.

The process

A guided conversation that builds a reusable baseline.

  1. 01

    Set the boundary

    Choose a quick orientation or deeper baseline, review privacy, and decide what information is appropriate to share.

  2. 02

    Explore the business

    Answer one adaptive question at a time about customers, value, work, economics, people, information, risks, and goals.

  3. 03

    Approve the baseline

    Review facts, assumptions, unknowns, strengths, conflicts, and opportunities before they become the basis for recommendations.

  4. 04

    Consider the next step

    Receive advisory recommendations with clear uncertainty, human decision points, success measures, and a reversible first experiment.

Choose your depth

Begin where your time and decisions require.

You can move from one path to another later. The quick option is intentionally provisional.

Evidence-backed assessment

Add document review, multiple participants, conflict resolution, privacy decisions, and validation of material claims.

Deeper review

Why preparation matters

The tool is rarely the whole problem—or the whole solution.

Research does not establish one universal AI-project failure rate. It does consistently identify unclear business problems, weak data, poor workflow fit, insufficient ownership, and inadequate operating preparation as recurring barriers to value.

Read the evidence and limitations →
74% of companies in BCG's 2024 study had not yet demonstrated tangible AI value.
37% of respondents in McKinsey's 2026 survey reported positive enterprise-level EBIT contribution from AI.
84% of RAND's industry interviewees cited leadership-driven causes among primary reasons AI projects fail.

Privacy

The framework may be public. Your business information should not be.

Choose a processing environment deliberately. A private hosted workspace is not the same as fully local processing. Share only information you are authorized to use, minimize sensitive details, and keep approved checkpoints in storage the business controls.

Advisory use

Free guidance, not the only decision factor.

This is a free, limited-scope service. It cannot guarantee success and should not replace qualified financial, legal, security, or operational review when consequences are significant.

Start the conversation

Download, load, and begin.

No application or API integration is required for the first test. Download the framework, add its files to a private AI project, and use the included setup guide.

Common questions

A few things to know before you begin.

Will this judge how I have run my business?

No. The process is designed to acknowledge strengths and progress while creating an honest baseline for future decisions.

Do I have to finish in one sitting?

No. Ask the consultant to create a resume checkpoint whenever you stop. Save the approved checkpoint so you can continue reliably later.

Does the framework decide which AI system I should buy?

No. It helps clarify use cases, requirements, risks, and priorities. The owner and authorized decision-makers remain responsible for consequential decisions.

Can it be used with a local AI model?

Yes, but fully local processing requires local inference, document handling, retrieval, storage, and network controls—not merely a locally installed chat model.
